To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the threshold of motion is determined by the maximum shear stress in the flow and that the threshold of particle motion can be described in terms of the Keulegan–Carpenter number.
the threshold of motion of sand particles is determined by the combined effects of bed fluid drag/lift and bed fluid acceleration.

the threshold of motion for coarse particles under regular waves is determined by the maximum shear stress in the flow and that this shear stress is a result of drag/lift forces as well as bed fluid acceleration.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the initiation of motion of coarse sediment particles in regular waves.
the initiation of motion of a coarse particle under the action of regular shoaling waves.
the initiation of motion of coarse sediments under regular shoaling wave conditions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the initiation of motion is due to a combined effect of drag/lift force and bed fluid acceleration, but the exact formulation of the coefficients for drag and acceleration is still an open question.

the threshold of motion of non-cohesive particles in the presence of wave acceleration is a function of peak orbital velocity and intra-wave acceleration and the threshold of motion is close to the maximum of the sum of the two.
initiation of motion is a function of the peak orbital velocity and the peak acceleration, which is in line with Nielsen and Callaghan's (2003) formulation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the threshold of motion is not only determined by the maximum shear stress but also by the duration of the shear stress.

the threshold of motion for coarse particles under regular waves is not only a function of peak orbital velocity but also of bed fluid acceleration and that the effect of acceleration on the threshold is not well understood yet.
the initiation of motion is a very complex problem that is strongly related to the flow field around the particles.
The main takeaway from our work is that

for the case of regular waves with weak to moderate intra-wave accelerations the initiation of coarse particle motion occurs at the maximum shear stress, and that the initiation of motion is not affected by the presence or absence of an initial bed shear layer.
the initiation of coarse particle motion can be predicted by using the maximum shear stress as the criterion.
the threshold of motion of particles in a wave field is strongly dependent on the intra-wave bed fluid acceleration.
